text:
Noah Kim: Hi finance folks 1 — noticed a charge `HOTEL DCC 212.00` on my corp card from Dublin. The hotel printed a charge in EUR and the card processed a DCC USD amount. I only have the hotel folio (EUR 188.50) and the card statement showing 212.00 USD. Which amount do we reimburse?

expenses-bot: Automated note: DCC (dynamic currency conversion) transactions can lead to higher costs. Finance requires original merchant folio + card statement. If DCC applied, employees should submit the original in-local-currency invoice for reconciliation.

Priya Desai: @Noah please upload the hotel folio and the card transaction screenshot. We usually reimburse based on the original merchant currency (EUR) and convert at the companys daily FX rate, unless card policy suggests otherwise. Do you have proof the room was for client meetings?

Noah Kim: Uploaded folio (folio_ireland_0905.pdf) and screenshot of the card charge. Meeting with ACME PMs on 2024-09-05. Attached meeting invite screenshot as proof.

Priya Desai: OK thanks. We'll convert the EUR amount at the 2024-09-05 company FX rate and ignore the DCC USD amount. Finance will post an adjustment if necessary. @Liam can you confirm internal GL coding for client travel in EMEA?

Liam O'Connell: Use GL code TRV-EMEA-CLIENT and tag vendor as "Hotel - DCC dispute possible". I'll flag a note for AP to monitor similar hotel DCC charges this quarter; might be worth reaching out to travel vendor for guidance.

Noah Kim: Appreciate it 1. Anything else I should add to the Ramp expense?

Priya Desai: Please list the folio reference, arrival/departure dates, and attach the meeting invite. We'll process as EUR 188.50 -> converted at company FX. Expect reimbursement in next payroll cycle.

expenses-bot: Expense accepted for review. Reference EXP-9021.
